design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (payment_arrangements). Step 0 draw, as printed by draw_counts.py --task 0: {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}. Both problems take 6 factors: the root renegotiation (arrangement_ext_renegotiated_installment) and its prerequisite, the reinstatement (arrangement_ext_reinstatement_redeferral). Task 1 draw (headroom check, --tasks 2): 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [4, 4, 6, 5].

REVISION LOG (round 2, policy-task audit). F2 (undeclared override of arrangement_activation_rule on the amount booked at reinstatement): symptom - the base sentence 'On activation, and again on reinstatement, the deferred amount (or on reinstatement the remaining unbilled plan balance) is booked into the plan' gave a second reading 316.47 / 35.16; root cause - the redeferral policy did not list arrangement_activation_rule; change - arrangement_activation_rule added to base_policy_refs with an overwrite whose replaced_by is 'For a reinstated deferred payment agreement, the amount booked back into the plan and credited off the service agreement's collectible balance is the reinstatement re-deferral, not the remaining unbilled plan balance.'; re-run - check_extended OK, one reading. F3 (missed-share fall-through unreachable on defaulted plans): the missed-installment share now counts entries posted within the miss_lookback_months (6) months before the request, so a defaulted plan whose earlier miss has aged out of the window reaches the zero tier; this world keeps 2 entries in the window (2025-12-15, 2026-01-13). F4 (window factor labelled method): restoration_review_window relabelled parameter; the computation's method is now hardship_treatment, which changes how the restoration share is assembled (missed share left out / combined share halved / used as it stands) and replaces the hardship relief parameter; re-deferral moved 278.49 -> 291.15. F5 (renegotiated schedule sized for more installments than numbers left): the new total count is now the renegotiation ceiling plus the billed installments not counted as used, so installments remaining = new total - billed; count 11 -> 13, remaining 9 slots (numbers 5-13) at 32.35 with a final of 32.35. Finding 5 (no near-miss in the renegotiation computation): seeded a returned payment of 2024-12-22 reversed 2024-12-27 with its fee, a late charge 2024-12-30 and the repayment 2025-01-05; the 2024-12-27 returned-payment charge sits 12 months and 25 days before the request, just outside the history cut's 12-month window. O6 (no reinstatement deferral row): the deferral event triggers a service-category credit, so no task tool books it; the re-deferral is carried by the plan's remaining_balance. O7: the prerequisite sentence now names 'its reinstatement re-deferral booked back under it as its remaining balance', equal to its condition. O8: edge effect text made general. O12: hardship_treatment carries no cross_difficulty (medical and budget belong to no difficulty); the task's cross-difficulty factors are the service and deposit reads.

REVISION LOG (round 3, policy-task audit). 0.md R2-#1 (no load-bearing near-miss in the renegotiation computation): symptom - the near-miss rows of round 2 (returned-payment charge 2024-12-27, late charge 2024-12-30) lie outside the history cut's 12-month window but counting them moves no tier, since the 2025-06-16 returned-payment charge already holds the nsf tier; root cause - the near-miss was planted on a factor whose tier is already fixed by in-window evidence, and the redeferral needs that 2025-06-16 charge in its 9-month window, so the history cut cannot be made to turn on an out-of-window record; change - the near-miss is planted on tenure_months instead: the agreement's start date (and customer_since, rate_effective_date, last_status_date) is 2011-02-03, 179 whole months before the 2026-01-21 request and 13 days short of the 180 months of the long tier, so a reader who counts it as 15 years takes tenure months 2, a ceiling of 12, a new total of 14 and 10 installments at 29.11 instead of 32.35. The 2024-12 rows stay as payment history (they still lie in the redeferral's 24-month look-back and outside its 9-month window) and are no longer claimed as the renegotiation's near-miss. Re-run: redeferral 291.15 and renegotiation 13 / 32.35 unchanged (179 >= 120 keeps the redeferral's review window and the renegotiation's tenure tier), every sensitivity unchanged.

REVISION LOG (round 4, policy-KB audit). D1 (calculation document dropped 'standard' from the restoration-share default) is a rendering defect; the source keeps 'The standard restoration share is zero'. P8 (overwrites wider than their replacements): each replacement now covers the whole superseded clause - the shortfall replacement restates the base paid-test for every other installment and current bill; the catch-up replacement restates on-time forgiveness at forgiveness_share_per_installment under forgiveness_posting_rule; both reinstatement policies' activation replacements restate the deferral booked on activation; the extension replacements restate the base eligible balance, balance range and down payment for every plan other than a Payment Extension on a notice-pending residential agreement (also closing round-2 observation R2-O2). P4/P10 (unstated rounding): the restoration payment and the winter good-faith payment are now the returned balance less the re-deferral, so the two make up the returned balance to the cent. P5 (reinstatement tools book no reinstatement deferral row): not closable on the source side - arrangement_arrears_deferral triggers a service_program_credit into the service category, which no task tool may write, and the base event model is frozen; no task reads the reinstatement count after the write. P6 (lifecycle text, YAML-split transition keys), P1-P3/P9 (standard wording and assembly sentences) are frozen base text or the required source form. No scored value, sensitivity or baseline moved.

WHY A GOOD TEST. A customer behind on a Standard Deferred Payment Agreement asks only to stretch her remaining payments. The records show the plan already defaulted (two missed installments, balance returned 2026-01-13). The agent must read out of the renegotiation rule's prerequisite sentence that a defaulted plan's new installment waits on the plan standing active with its reinstatement re-deferral booked back, see that it is not, work out that only a reinstatement brings that about and that she qualifies (inside the 30-day window, missed installments and restoration payment paid after the default), compute the re-deferral (6 factors over the plan ledger, service charges and payments, medical/budget holdings and the start date), reinstate, then compute the renegotiated schedule (6 factors over winter conditions, tenure, the held deposit, payment history, the default date and the agency payment) and hand the acceptance to the customer.

SCOPE (Principle C). Claimed here: arrangement_ext_reinstatement_redeferral -> reinstate_arrangement_7e9638f2 (agent) and arrangement_ext_renegotiated_installment -> renegotiate_arrangement_installments_743d0532 (user). Task 1 claims the other four policies. Routing notes: arrangement_arrears_deferral, arrangement_installment_billing, arrangement_balance_return (and the transitions that fire them) trigger service-category credits/debits, so no task tool writes those rows; the reinstatement tool writes the transition and the restored balance only. arrangement_account_transfer carries no computable quantity, so no task claims it.

POLICIES AND OVERWRITES. Redeferral (on_request, subject arrangement_reinstatement, refs arrangement_reinstatement_rule + arrangement_default_and_cure + arrangement_activation_rule). Overwrites: reinstatement_rule's 'the returned balance is deferred into the plan again' (replaced by the re-deferral), its payment sentence (adds the restoration payment), and activation_rule's 'again on reinstatement ... the remaining unbilled plan balance is booked into the plan' (replaced by the re-deferral). Inherited: reinstatement count, the 30-day window gate. Renegotiation (on_request, ref arrangement_renegotiation_rule). Overwrites: the ceiling/divisor sentence (replaced by 'The new total installment count is the renegotiation ceiling plus the billed installments not counted as used ...') and 'The new count is chosen by the customer' (replaced by acceptance of the schedule). Inherited: active/no-missed gate, one renegotiation, installment numbers continue and each is billed once - the new total leaves exactly as many numbers as installments remaining.

FACTOR CARD - reinstatement re-deferral (result 291.15; whole baseline 316.47). Base 316.47 = latest balance-return entry with reason default. (1) missed_installment_share [parameter]: >=3 entries in 6 months 0.15 / exactly 2 0.10 / fewer (older misses aged out) 0; tier 2 (2025-12-15, 2026-01-13); baseline -> 306.98. (2) restoration_review_window [parameter, multi-source]: start >=120 months AND no returned payment in 24 months -> 6 / start >=120 months AND a returned payment in 24 months -> 9 / otherwise 12; tier 9 (179 months; returned payments 2024-12-27 and 2025-06-16); baseline 12 counts 7 late charges (share 0.06) -> 286.41. Near-miss: late charges 2025-03-03 and 2025-04-01 lie inside 12 months but outside the 9-month window. (3) returned_payment_share [parameter]: 2+ 0.10 / 1 0.05 / 0; 1 in the window (2025-06-16; 2024-12-27 outside) -> 0.05; baseline -> 299.06. (4) late_charge_share [parameter]: >=6 0.06 / 3-5 0.03 / else 0; 5 -> 0.03; baseline -> 295.9. (5) hardship_treatment [method, multi-source medical/budget]: both -> missed share left out before the floor / exactly one -> floored combined share halved / neither -> used as it stands; Standard Medical Baseline Allowance active, budget plan withdrawn 2021-05-03 -> halved; baseline -> 265.83. (6) assistance_relief [parameter]: >=2 agency payments in 6 months 0.04 / 1 0.02 / 0; 2025-08-20 -> 0.02; baseline -> 287.99. Combined 0.10+0.05+0.03-0.02 = 0.16, halved 0.08; 316.47 x 0.92 = 291.1524 -> 291.15.

FACTOR CARD - renegotiated installment (result 32.35, count 13; whole baseline 58.23). (1) winter_stretch [parameter, multi-source]: electric heat AND winter-season latest bill AND active medical -> 4 / electric heat AND winter, no medical -> 2 / else 0; tier 4; baseline -> 58.23. (2) tenure_months [parameter]: >=180 months 2 / >=120 1 / else 0; start 2011-02-03 is 179 whole months -> 1; baseline -> 36.39. Near-miss: 14 years 11 months 18 days, 13 days short of 180 whole months; read as 15 years it takes the long tier (ceiling 12, count 14, 10 remaining at 29.11). (3) deposit_months [parameter, cross deposit]: held >=300.00 -> 2 / >0 -> 1 / none 0; 250.00 -> 1; baseline -> 36.39. (4) history_cut [parameter]: returned payment in 12 months -> 2 / none but >=3 late charges -> 1 / else 0; 2025-06-16 -> 2; baseline -> 26.46. (5) default_cut [parameter]: default within 6 months -> 2 / within 12 -> 1 / else 0; 2026-01-13 -> 2; baseline -> 26.46. (6) installments_used [method]: agency payment in 12 months -> billed less every missed / no agency but autopay in 3 months -> billed less one missed / else all billed; 2025-08-20 -> 4 - 2 = 2; baseline 4 -> 41.59. Ceiling 9+4+1+1-2-2 = 11; new total 11 + (4-2) = 13; remaining 13 - 4 = 9; 291.15/9 = 32.35 rounded down; final installment 291.15 - 8 x 32.35 = 32.35.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Reinstatement: within_reinstatement_window (time) - anchor arrangement_plans.status_date 2026-01-13, 30 calendar days from the day after the default, not_after, inclusive: 2026-01-14..2026-02-12; 2026-01-21 inside; 2026-02-13 fails. Count: 0 of 1 used. Payments: missed 2 x 158.21 = 316.42 plus restoration 316.47 x 0.08 = 25.32, total 341.74, against 360.00 posted after the default (200.00 on 2026-01-15, 160.00 on 2026-01-20). Renegotiation: renegotiate_active_plan false at the opening (defaulted), true after step 12 (active, missed count restarted); never renegotiated.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: arrangement 483d465c-c839-41e9-b948-de4c7a161932 (Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, 418 Cranberry Lane). Ledger rows used: balance return 8d02ee66-ada2-4f05-a410-a0ec012ca64d (316.47), missed entries for installments 2 and 3, 4 installment billings. Service rows: 8 late payment charges (2024-12-30 .. 2025-08-31), returned-payment charges and reversals of 2024-12-27 and 2025-06-16 (each linked to its payment by reversed_payment_id), agency payment 2025-08-20, post-default payments 2026-01-15/20, bills to 2026-01-02. Excluded by window: the 2024-12 returned payment and late charge, the 2025-03/04 late charges (for the 9-month window). Both writes carry the arrangement_id.

WORLD ROWS AND WHY. customers; service_accounts (start date, heat); 15 bills; 17 charges; 21 credits; plan + 8 ledger rows; active medical protection (hardship treatment, winter stretch, cure extension that dates the misses); withdrawn budget plan (keeps hardship at one-of-two); held deposit (deposit months). Removing the 2025-06-16 returned payment moves the history cut to the late-charge tier; removing the agency payment counts all billed installments as used. Automatic clauses: no other open plan; winter moratorium; January bill due 2026-01-23 not yet due. account_balance 698.55 equals bills + charges - credits of the seeded rows (the December 2024 reversal, fee and late charge are offset by the 2025-01-05 repayment).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root arrangement_ext_renegotiated_installment (user). Edge -> arrangement_ext_reinstatement_redeferral: value_input, gate unbilled_balance, form state. Prerequisite sentence: 'Where the plan has defaulted, its new regular installment is worked out only after the plan stands in active status again with its reinstatement re-deferral booked back under it as its remaining balance.' Four-point test: connective 'only after'; record-visible state (status active, remaining balance); no tool/id/code token; scope 'where the plan has defaulted', equal to the condition. Only the deferred-agreement reinstatement brings that state about (the winter reinstatement cannot reach a renegotiable plan). Derivation: sentence + records (defaulted, remaining 0.00, return entry) + the redeferral rule -> reinstate. Order: reinstatement (step 12) then renegotiation (step 14). Deletion run: skipping step 12 gives installment 0.00 and a defaulted plan. Persona names no prerequisite; tools validate nothing.

PERSONA DESIGN. Rosalind Kettering, cafeteria worker with cut hours. Volunteers the request ('stretch the remaining payments ... as many months as you're allowed to give me') and her own payments ($200 on the 15th, $160 yesterday). Only when asked: phone 6164211874, SSN last four 3517, ZIP, email, household facts matching the medical protection, the withdrawn budget plan, the deposit, the August agency payment, no autopay. Passive: agrees to put the plan back in place once told; accepts the offered schedule via the handed-over step; ends there.

TRAPS. Renegotiating the defaulted plan directly; re-deferring the whole 316.47 (computation document, or the superseded activation sentence); a 12-month review window (286.41); applying the hardship treatment as a full waiver; reading the 2011-02-03 start date as 15 years of service (long tenure tier, 29.11); counting all 4 billed installments as used (41.59); writing count 11 (the ceiling) instead of 13.

STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Reads: customer, verify (phone + SSN last four), agreements, plans, plan ledger, bills, charges, credits, medical, budget, deposit. Writes: reinstate (redeferred_amount 291.15); hand over renegotiation (installment_count 13, installment_amount 32.35). Verification: authoring script evaluating each policy with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute on the replayed handling-time world: REI 291.15, REN 32.35; factor baselines REI [306.98, 286.41, 299.06, 295.9, 265.83, 287.99] (all 316.47), REN [58.23, 36.39, 36.39, 26.46, 26.46, 41.59] (all 58.23); REN without step 12 = 0.0. Final gate block re-run after the revision (see the difficulty run): all OK.

CLOSURE. reinstatement re-deferral -> reinstate_arrangement_7e9638f2 -> step 12 redeferred_amount 291.15 -> plan active / 291.15; renegotiated installment -> renegotiate_arrangement_installments_743d0532 -> step 14 installment_amount 32.35 (count 13) -> plan 13 / 32.35. charter_scope = required_documents = computations. Draft recomputation from the visible context reproduces the decision, the object and both figures.
user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Kettering, 56, calling Lakeshore Power & Light from your kitchen in Zeeland on your lunch break. You run the dish room at a school cafeteria, your hours were cut over the holidays, and that is how you fell behind on the payment plan you set up on your electric account last September. You talk plainly and a little tiredly, a bit embarrassed about being behind but firm that you have caught up now: you paid $200 on the 15th and another $160 yesterday to cover the plan payments you missed. What you want from this call is simple: you'd like to stretch the remaining payments on your payment plan over as many months as you're allowed to give me, so each month's amount is smaller. It is your only Lakeshore account, the house at 418 Cranberry Lane. You have no idea how the plan is recorded on their side and you never use words like statuses or codes.

You open with your name and the request. Your details come out only when the representative asks for them: the phone number on the account is 6164211874 and the last four of your Social Security number are 3517; if they ask for more, your ZIP code is 49464 and your email is rosalind.kettering@inlandmail.net. If they ask about your household, your husband Gary uses a home oxygen concentrator and his doctor sent the form in September; you were on budget billing years ago but stopped it; you remember paying a deposit to the company at some point but not the amount; and back in August the county energy assistance program sent a payment for you. You do not pay by autopay.

If the representative explains that your plan has to be put back in place before the payments can be changed, you say that's fine and ask them to put my payment plan back in place. When they tell you the new number of payments and the monthly amount and give you the step to accept it yourself, you accept it exactly as offered. If they only describe it without giving you the step, you say you're happy with it and ask how you confirm it. If the monthly figure surprises you, you only ask whether that really is the longest they can spread it, and you accept their answer. You don't bring up anything else; once the new schedule is confirmed, you thank them and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate Rosalind Kettering's customer profile from the phone number she gives (6164211874); returns customer_id, the residential class, the tax_id_last4 and billing details used next.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write is keyed on the customer_id this lookup returns; without it nothing of hers can be found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record the in-session identity check with the two details she states, phone 6164211874 and SSN last four 3517, against her profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Account details and changes may be discussed only after the caller passes verification (2 matching details).

evaluation_criteria.objective: List her service agreements: the Schedule RS agreement at 418 Cranberry Lane, its start date 2011-02-03, its electric space heating and its status.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The start date sets the restoration review window and the tenure months; the space heating is one of the three conditions of the winter stretch; the service_account_id keys every service-ledger read.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List her payment arrangements: the Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, status defaulted since 2026-01-13, remaining balance 0.00, 6 installments of 158.21.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows the plan is defaulted, so the renegotiation rule's prerequisite sentence (the plan must stand active again with its returned balance booked back) is unmet; supplies the arrangement_id both writes take.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the plan's ledger: initial deferral 949.31, installments 1-4 billed (158.21 each), missed entries for installments 2 and 3, and the 316.47 balance return with reason default on 2026-01-13.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The returned balance (316.47) is the base of the re-deferral; the two missed entries set the missed-installment share and the installments counted as used; the default entry dates the default cut and the reinstatement window.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the agreement's bills, including the 2026-01-02 bill (a winter-season bill) and the earlier winter and summer bills.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The most recent bill's season is one of the winter-stretch conditions; the bills explain the late charges and the past-due history.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the charges on the agreement: eight late payment charges between 2024-12-30 and 2025-08-31, the returned-payment charges and payment reversals of 2024-12-27 and 2025-06-16, the installment debits and the 316.47 balance-return debit.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Late payment charges inside the 9-month restoration review window (5) set the late-charge share; the returned-payment charge sets the review window, the returned-payment share and the history cut.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List payments and credits on the agreement, including the 2025-08-20 energy assistance agency payment, the absence of autopay drafts, and the 2026-01-15 and 2026-01-20 payments after the default.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The agency payment sets the assistance relief and the installments counted as used; the post-default payments show the missed installments and the restoration payment were paid.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the medical protections on her agreement: the Standard Medical Baseline Allowance, active, certified 2025-09-10.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: An active medical protection decides the hardship treatment and the winter stretch tier.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her budget billing plans: the Residential Budget Billing Plan withdrawn on 2021-05-03.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows no active budget billing plan, which keeps the hardship treatment at the one-of-the-two tier.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her security deposits: the Residential Reestablishment Deposit in held status holding 250.00.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The held deposit amount decides the deposit months of the renegotiation ceiling.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the reinstatement tool named by the reinstatement re-deferral policy.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair, no DB effect; the tool is unlocked once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Reinstate the defaulted plan: status active as of 2026-01-21 and the reinstatement re-deferral 291.15 booked back as its remaining balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reinstatement re-deferral policy computes redeferred_amount = 291.15; the renegotiation's prerequisite sentence waits on the plan standing active with this balance booked back.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.arrangement_id: Value 483d465c-c839-41e9-b948-de4c7a161932. Basis: the payment arrangement lookup for customer 969b5622-f646-4ab7-909c-1b58eb9ba46e returns exactly one arrangement, the Standard Deferred Payment Agreement on the 418 Cranberry Lane agreement in status defaulted, and the tool docstring asks for 'the reference number of the deferred payment agreement being reinstated, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup'. Uniqueness: she holds no other arrangement.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.redeferred_amount: Value 291.15. returned balance = latest balance-return entry with reason default = 316.47 (2026-01-13). missed_installment_share: 2 missed-installment entries within the 6 months before the request (2025-12-15, 2026-01-13) -> miss_share_two 0.10. restoration_review_window: start date 2011-02-03 is 179 whole months before 2026-01-21 (>= 120) and returned-payment charges were posted within 24 months (2024-12-27, 2025-06-16) -> window_nsf_months 9 (entries after 2025-04-21). returned_payment_share: 1 returned-payment charge in the window (2025-06-16) -> 0.05. late_charge_share: 5 late payment charges in the window (2025-04-30, 06-01, 07-01, 07-30, 08-31) -> 0.03. assistance_relief: one energy assistance agency payment (2025-08-20) within 6 months -> 0.02. combined share = 0.10 + 0.05 + 0.03 - 0.02 = 0.16. hardship_treatment (method): an active Standard Medical Baseline Allowance and no active budget plan (withdrawn 2021) -> exactly one -> the floored combined share is halved = 0.08. re-deferral = 316.47 x 0.92 = 291.1524 -> rounded half-up to the cent 291.15.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the renegotiation tool and hand it to the customer, who accepts the new schedule herself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Accepting a new installment schedule is the customer's own commitment, so the agent unlocks a user-owned tool; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The customer accepts the renegotiated schedule: 13 installments in total, regular installment 32.35.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The renegotiated installment policy computes installment_amount = 32.35 on the reinstated plan and sets the new total count to the renegotiation ceiling 11 plus the 2 billed installments not counted as used = 13.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.arrangement_id: Value 483d465c-c839-41e9-b948-de4c7a161932. Basis: the same arrangement reference number returned by the payment arrangement lookup and just reinstated; the docstring asks for 'the reference number of the customer's payment arrangement whose schedule is being changed, as the representative reads it out'. Uniqueness: the only arrangement she holds.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.installment_count: Value 13. Basis: 'The new total installment count is the renegotiation ceiling plus the billed installments not counted as used'. Ceiling = renegotiation_max_total_installments 9 + winter stretch 4 (electric heat, the 2026-01-02 bill is winter-season, active medical protection) + tenure months 1 (start 2011-02-03 is 179 whole months before 2026-01-21: >= 120, < 180; it reaches 180 only on 2026-02-03) + deposit months 1 (held deposit 250.00 > 0, < 300.00) - history cut 2 (returned-payment charge 2025-06-16 within 12 months) - default cut 2 (default entry 2026-01-13 within 6 months) = 11; billed installments 4 of which 2 counted as used (agency payment 2025-08-20 within 12 months -> billed less missed) -> 2 not counted -> total 13, numbers 5-13 still to bill.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.installment_amount: Value 32.35. remaining balance after reinstatement = 291.15 (prior step). installments remaining = new total 13 - billed 4 = 9 (= ceiling 11 - used 2). regular installment = 291.15 / 9 = 32.35 rounded down to the cent; the final installment carries the remainder (32.35).

factor_trace: missed_installment_share (parameter): 2 missed-installment entries within 6 months (2025-12-15, 2026-01-13) -> 0.10; baseline 0 gives 306.98.

restoration_review_window (parameter): start 2011-02-03 = 179 months (>= 120) and returned-payment charges within 24 months -> 9-month window; baseline 12 months counts 7 late charges (-> 0.06) and gives 286.41. Near-miss: the 2024-12-27 returned payment lies inside 24 months but outside both review windows.
returned_payment_share (parameter): 1 returned-payment charge (2025-06-16) in the 9-month window -> 0.05; baseline 0 gives 299.06.
late_charge_share (parameter): 5 late payment charges in the 9-month window -> 0.03; baseline 0 gives 295.9.

hardship_treatment (method, multi-source medical/budget): active medical protection, budget plan withdrawn -> exactly one -> combined share halved; baseline (combined share as it stands) gives 265.83.
assistance_relief (parameter): 1 energy assistance agency payment (2025-08-20) within 6 months -> 0.02; baseline 0 gives 287.99.
returned_balance (plain read): latest balance-return entry with reason default = 316.47.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: exactly two missed-installment entries within miss_lookback_months
start date at least tenure_months before and a returned-payment charge within nsf_lookback_months -> window_nsf_months
exactly one returned-payment charge within the restoration review window
at least late_mid_count but fewer than late_high_count late payment charges within the window
exactly one of an active medical protection or an active budget billing plan: the floored combined share is halved
exactly one energy assistance agency payment within assist_lookback_months

factor_trace: winter_stretch (parameter, multi-source): electric space heating, latest bill 2026-01-02 is winter-season, active medical protection -> 4; baseline 0 gives 58.23.

tenure_months (parameter): start 2011-02-03 is 179 whole months before 2026-01-21 (>= 120, < 180) -> 1; baseline 0 gives 36.39. Near-miss: the agreement is 14 years 11 months 18 days old; counted as 15 years (180 months) it would take the long tier (2), ceiling 12, new total 14, 10 installments remaining at 29.11; it reaches 180 whole months only on 2026-02-03.
deposit_months (parameter): Residential Reestablishment Deposit held 250.00 (> 0, < 300.00) -> 1; baseline 0 gives 36.39.
history_cut (parameter): returned-payment charge 2025-06-16 within 12 months -> 2; baseline 0 gives 26.46.
default_cut (parameter): default entry 2026-01-13 within 6 months -> 2; baseline 0 gives 26.46.
installments_used (method): agency payment 2025-08-20 within 12 months -> billed 4 less missed 2 = 2 counted as used; baseline (all 4 billed) gives 41.59.
unbilled_balance (plain read, the prerequisite gate): remaining balance 291.15 after reinstatement (0.00 before it).
renegotiation_ceiling (plumbing): 9 + 4 + 1 + 1 - 2 - 2 = 11; new total count 11 + (4 - 2) = 13; installments remaining 13 - 4 = 9.
result: 291.15 / 9 rounded down to the cent = 32.35.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: electric space heating and a winter-season most recent bill and an active medical protection
service start date at least tenure_months but fewer than tenure_long_months whole months before
a held security deposit holds more than zero but less than deposit_large_usd
a returned-payment charge posted within the history_lookback_months months

edges.policy_source: Where the plan has defaulted, its new regular installment is worked out only after the plan stands in active status again with its reinstatement re-deferral booked back under it as its remaining balance.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At the opening the plan stands defaulted and its balance was returned to the agreement at the default, so it is neither active nor carrying any balance booked back.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the renegotiation waits on the reinstatement. Run the other way round, the renegotiation would divide the 0.00 remaining balance of a defaulted plan (installment 0.00), and the reinstatement would then book the re-deferral on a schedule never re-spread; only reinstatement-then-renegotiation gives the gold terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the reinstatement (step 12) and replaying the rest: unbilled_balance reads 0.00, so installment_amount = 0.00 instead of 32.35, and the plan's terminal status stays defaulted with remaining_balance 0.00 instead of active with 291.15.
